correctness.rationale: Three unit phases sum to zero only when they are a rotated set of cube roots. Applying this to all row differences makes the ternary depths complementary and requires the nonternary products to vanish. For eligible A, putting g=gcd(N,a1-a0,a2-a0) and L=N/(3g), B chooses one point from each of the three residue classes modulo 3L above a chosen residue modulo L. This gives Lg^3 distinct unordered spectra. Independent ternary row lifts and nonternary all-congruent counts give the stated strata, with a single division by six for globally distinct ordered triples; multiplying by the spectrum multiplicity and summing produces the total. Read the frozen RESULT.md, VERIFICATION.md, verify.py and verification_output.txt. Independently tested all three row-pair orthogonalities and fixed-A counts for 13 orders, including 27 and 36, via python /workspace/audit_replay.py 4; complete replay output is /workspace/review-evidence/4.txt.
residual_risks: Finite replay supports, but does not establish, the all-modulus identity.
The wording 'even when they coincide' is potentially ambiguous in isolation: the ordered-pair convention and formulas count a diagonal pair once, not twice.

evidence: Theorem 3.6 decides every concrete ordered pair of unordered triples at every cyclic order. Malikiosis supplies a broader difference/zero-set criterion, while An–Lai concern spectral measures and product-form triples.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The already exact local pairwise conditions from Theorem 3.6 determine the concrete aggregate through elementary fiber sizes. General spectral-set theory on its own would not settle this arithmetic enumeration.

evidence: For an eligible row triple, Theorem 3.6 written in differences means columns share a residue mod L=N/(3g) and occupy all three lifts modulo 3L; each lift has g elements. At row depth r there are 3^r shared residues and one choice from each of the three next-deeper classes, of size 3^(a-r-1). For each nonternary p, subtract two successive counts of ordered all-congruent triples, p^(3b-2k).
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Multiplying the residue-class sizes gives the fixed-row formula directly. Independent prime factors, then the elementary weighted sum (constant contribution at each ternary depth and at each nonterminal nonternary depth), give the other two formulas without a further structural theorem. This is a direct corollary of stronger prior coverage.
searches: Herr–Wiegand arXiv:1909.13145 PDF p. 19, Theorem 3.6 and proof

evidence: Herr–Wiegand give an if-and-only-if criterion on the primitive sets of both triples. For a nonzero difference d, the corresponding primitive order is N/gcd(N,d); its p-adic valuation is the complement of the truncated valuation of d.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The prior min/max ternary sums force the two ranges individually to collapse and give row and column depths summing to a-1. The other-prime inequalities give the complementary lower bounds on all column difference valuations. This is the same complete pair relation, not just a common existence test.

evidence: The distinct same-day 3p record counts minor ranks, not orthogonality among rank-three minors. The October 11 consecutive-triple record gives exactly N/3 spectra for A={0,1,2} when 3 divides N, via ratio-one minimizers. Herr–Wiegand's G(180,3) graph is not the requested aggregate table.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: There is one exact special-case count; the rank census does not cover the larger claim and same-day metadata do not determine priority. The fail rests on the mathematical implication from the preceding pair criterion rather than on finding a printed copy of the table.

originality.rationale: Covered by direct counting from the stronger pairwise valuation classification in Herr–Wiegand, Theorem 3.6. The closed formulas need not appear there for this conclusion: translating the exact criterion makes the fibers three independent choices in equal-sized residue classes, and the remaining histogram is the elementary census of residue-depth strata. No new compatibility principle or nonmechanical counting step is required. This is implication-based coverage, not evidence that the earlier paper explicitly prints the histogram.
residual_risks: Ranked local search is not exhaustive; broader primary-literature search was deferred. Neither limits the concrete implication from Theorem 3.6.
No assertion that Herr–Wiegand print the aggregate formulas or that any same-day record has chronological precedence.
